title: Finders Tell Their Friends
logline: A jungle of entrepreneurial opportunity sits under a floating protopian island called Founder Heaven. The only way up is camouflaged space elevators that carry everyone who reaches them, until the day each one goes dark forever, and nobody below knows when or why. The island's keepers want the cars full before the dark comes, so they drop small orange compasses into the jungle that point toward the live elevator. Maya works harder than anyone, misses an elevator by following a myth, watches a prophet's broadcast arrive after the dark, and learns the one thing the myths and the smudged advice never say: the seekers who make it in time hold a compass and have friends who clue them in the moment they find one. She joins a small circle that shares maps honestly, rides up with her friends, and tells it straight from above.
spineNote: The argued object is WHY HARD WORK ALONE DOES NOT BEAT THE DARK. Three false channels are examined and dismissed in order (myth from below, mistranslated stories from above, broadcast from a prophet), and the true channel is demonstrated rather than asserted: a compass from the keepers in hand and a small circle whose rule is that whoever finds it tells the others first. The coda closes the loop the false channels opened: the ones who ride up owe the ground a story told straight. REVISED 2026-08-08 (Gary): capacity is never scarce (an elevator carries everyone who reaches it); the urgency is the unexplained dark; the keepers' orange compasses are the true help from above, paired against the smudged pages.

beats.text: There is a jungle where the hopeful go. It is green and loud and alive, and it does not care how good your plan is. Everyone who walks in is looking for the same thing: a way up.
beats.provenance: Gary's commission brief, 2026-08-07: 'a wild jungle of entrepreneurial opportunity, full of dangers, where hopefuls search for a way up'.

beats.text: Up is an island in the sky. It floats above the canopy in plain view, near enough to see its gardens and its bright machines, too far for any tree to reach. The people below call it Founder Heaven.
beats.provenance: Brief: 'FOUNDER HEAVEN, an aerial floating futuristic protopian island'.

beats.text: There is one way up. Elevators stand in the jungle, silver threads running from the forest floor to the island, and every one of them is camouflaged. You can cut a trail past one at arm's length and never know.
beats.provenance: Brief: 'the only way up is space elevators, and they are completely camouflaged'.

beats.text: An elevator carries everyone who reaches it. The doors open for a crowd and for the one who comes alone. But one day, for reasons nobody below understands, an elevator goes dark, forever. Nobody knows which day. The hopefuls call the time it is alive a takeoff window. The jungle does not post it anywhere.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: capacity is NOT scarce; the elevator carries everyone who reaches it. The urgency is that an elevator goes dark, forever, for reasons nobody below understands, on a day nobody knows. 'Takeoff window' kept as the hopefuls' name for the time it is alive. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: When an elevator dies, the people who missed it gather at its feet and tell stories about the ones who made it up in time. The stories grow taller every season. That is how myths get written: by the people still on the ground.
beats.provenance: Brief: 'after an elevator dies, the people below write myths about the founders who made it up in time'.

beats.text: The founders up top tell stories too, and send them down. The pages fall a long way, and they land smudged into advice that points at nothing. So the island's keepers send something surer. They drop small orange compasses into the green, and every needle swings toward the live elevator. The keepers want the cars full before the dark comes.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: the compass beat. The island's keepers (never named as any real company) want as many seekers as possible to ride up before the dark comes, and airdrop small orange compasses that point toward the live elevator. Paired against the smudged pages: false help and true help fall from the same sky. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: Maya works harder than anyone in the jungle. She is up before the light, she carries her work everywhere, and she clears more trail in a week than most camps clear in a season. Hard work is her plan. She is sure it is enough.
beats.provenance: Brief arc: 'one seeker who works harder than everyone'.

beats.text: She follows the most famous myth in the jungle to the place where a great elevator once stood. It is exactly where the story said. It is covered in moss, and it has been dark for years. The myth was true. It was just finished.
beats.provenance: Brief arc: 'misses an elevator by following a myth'.

beats.text: One day a famous prophet arrives, and a million followers arrive behind him. He climbs the tallest rock and announces the location of a live elevator to everyone at once. He is not lying. But nobody knows how long any elevator will stay lit, and by the time anything can be announced to a million people, this one has gone dark, or the dark is too close. Broadcast means too late.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: the prophet still is not lying; his broadcast now arrives after this elevator has gone dark or too close to it, because nobody knows how long any elevator stays lit. Broadcast means too late. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: That night Maya counts every founder she has ever known who made it up. Not one of them found their elevator in a myth or an announcement. Each one had a friend who found it and told them first, quietly, the same hour. Finders tell their friends.
beats.provenance: Brief moral: 'the seekers who make it are the ones whose friends clue them in the moment they find one'.

beats.text: So she stops searching alone. She finds Chrissy, who lights up when she has something to share, and the engineer, who says plainly what he knows and what he does not. They draw their maps honestly, dead ends and all. A compass from the sky sits on the map where all three can read it, and they keep one rule: whoever finds it tells the others first.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: the circle now holds a compass from the sky beside the honest maps; a compass in hand plus a friend who tells you first is how you make it in time. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: It is Chrissy who finds it, on an ordinary morning, where the needle pointed, behind a curtain of vines she almost did not pull back. She does not climb a rock. She does not gather a crowd. She turns around and goes to get her friends.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: one clause added ('where the needle pointed') so the find follows the compass the circle keeps; the vines still nearly hide it, which is the camouflage's power. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: The doors are open and the light inside is warm, and there is room for every friend who comes. The jungle lets go of them trail by trail, and the island comes up like a sunrise.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: seat scarcity removed; there is room for every friend who comes. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: Founder Heaven is smaller than the myths and kinder than the smudged advice. And nearly everyone who stands there arrived the same way: holding a map a friend drew.
beats.provenance: Brief: protopian island, plus the moral generalized from the arrival side.

beats.text: Maya remembers the pages that fall and smudge. So she writes her story plainly and checks every word before she sends it down. I worked hard, and hard work was not enough. I held a compass from the sky, and a friend found the way and told me first. Work hard. Hold your compass. Find the friends who would tell you. Be one back.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: the moral gains the compass: work hard, hold your compass, find the friends who would tell you, be one back. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)

beats.text: Somewhere below, a hopeful reads a page that finally says what happened. So work hard. Keep a compass where you can reach it. Make sure the right people know your name when they find a silver thread in the green. Finders tell their friends. And the ones who ride up tell it straight.
beats.provenance: Gary's revision, 2026-08-08: the coda gains the compass: keep a compass where you can reach it; finders tell their friends; the ones who ride up tell it straight. (Prior text and provenance: see git history.)
